key_insight: Different flow paths can produce the exact same flow matching objective but very different SGD variance and convergence speed.
engineering_relevance: Choosing the transport path is an optimization lever for making generative flow models train faster without changing the target distribution.
method: Analyze gradient variance across the class of paths that preserve the same marginals and velocity field.
Derive an optimal linear path for a one-dimensional Gaussian case and a general variance-minimization formulation (PathOptθ).
Reformulate the path constraint into sample-estimable conditions so paths can be searched numerically.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theory plus experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixtures, and real datasets to validate the variance-reduction effect.
watch_item: The variance-optimal path must still satisfy the same marginal/velocity constraint; ignoring that constraint can reduce variance on paper but worsen actual convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
